subject: Renewal: premium support pathway and latency commitments
messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@datawave.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: DataWave Ops <ops@datwave.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation: support pathway and latency commitments

Connor —

Quick context: our annual contract with Redwood is up for renewal (Dec 15). Our usage has increased ~2.8x year-over-year and we plan to expand the number of product features backed by your API next quarter. Before we get into procurement, we need clarity on the following so I can build the internal case: 

- Premium SLA options available at renewal (what are specific uptime & latency SLOs you can promise for our workload?)
- Support tier changes: 24/7 priority on-call, escalation windows, runbook access, and who will be our primary technical contact
- Dedicated capacity / burst guarantees during peak campaigns and any crediting model for sustained incidents
- Pricing impact and discounts for committed spend / longer term (12/24 month)

If you can send a short mutual action plan and a one-page summary of the SLA addendum we can present to Procurement and Ops, that would be perfect. We expect procurement to ask for a P1 response SLA (target acknowledge/2hr, mitigation timeline) and a p99 latency target for inference — we'd like to understand whether you can commit to a p99 for our median sequence length (~480 tokens) and what that number looks like with/without dedicated capacity.

Can we also schedule a 30-minute QBR next week to walk through the proposal? I can invite our procurement lead and infra manager (David Liu).

Thanks — Priya

Priya Menon
Head of Platform Operations | DataWave
priya.menon@datawave.com
ops@datwave.com

Attachments referenced: current-month usage/export (we'll share a CSV in follow-up)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@datawave.com>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@datawave.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: support pathway and latency commitments

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask and congrats on the growth — excited to support the expansion. High-level proposal below; I've attached a draft SLA addendum and a usage mapping workbook so Procurement/Finance can see price/consumption sensitivity.

1) Premium SLA (renewal addendum):
   - Uptime: 99.95% platform availability (excludes scheduled maintenance)
   - Priority support: 24/7 priority on-call with P1 acknowledgement target: 30 minutes; P1 mitigation cadence and status updates every 2 hours until resolution
   - Latency SLO (dedicated pool): p99 <= 250ms for average request size (480 tokens) when routed to dedicated capacity. Non-dedicated routing p99 target: <= 450ms.

2) Dedicated capacity & burst guarantees:
   - Commitment tier: reserved pool sized to expected sustained qps with automatic 20% burst buffer for campaign windows
   - If sustained 20% overcommit for >6 hours, we provide incident credits (pro-rated) and immediate routing to overflow capacity where possible

3) Pricing & credits:
   - Price uplift for Premium SLA: ~20% over current hosted rate (reflects reserved capacity & priority staffing)
   - Commit discounts: 12-month commit = 15% discount on hosted token rates; 24-month = 20% discount
   - Incident crediting: service credits for SLA misses; migration credit: one-time $30k credit available by request

4) Next steps / timeline:
   - I'll send the SLA addendum (attached) and a one-pager mutual action plan.
   - Target: internal legal & procurement review completed by Nov 17; DocuSign by Nov 20 to allow operations lead time for capacity provisioning ahead of Jan 1 start date.

Attachments: 20261102-datawave-usage-mapping.xlsx; 20261103-premium-sla-addendum.docx

Would you be available for a 30-minute QBR Friday Nov 5 (10:00am PT) or Monday Nov 8 (2:00pm PT)? I can bring Laura (CS lead) to talk operational handoff.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: DataWave renewal — corroborate discounting & credits

Laura / Ben —

Forwarding Priya's inquiry and the proposed terms I shared. Quick asks so I can respond to Procurement with firm numbers: 

- Confirm the 15% commit discount for 12-month and 20% for 24-month (these are list-level asks from product/finance; are we comfortable with 15% on the table for >12 mo?)
- Incident crediting: I put a one-time $30k migration credit on the table. Approve?
- Latency statement: product has indicated 250ms p99 on dedicated for 480-token median is achievable on Ampere A1/P100-ish hardware; confirm with runtime team if we should phrase as target vs. guaranteed metric.

Pricing impact example (ballpark): if current spend = $120k/month, premium uplift (~20%) -> $144k/month; with 12-month 15% commit = $122.4k/month effective. Offering the $30k migration credit amortized over the first quarter helps procurement sign faster.

If you approve, I will:
1) Send the SLA addendum as a tracked DocuSign with the commit discount bracket called out
2) Offer a deployment kickoff window (2 weeks lead time after DocuSign) for capacity provisioning

Can you reply today so I can give Priya a definitive timeline?

Thanks — Connor

Cc: David Liu <david.liu@datawave.com>, DataWave Ops <ops@datwave.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: support pathway and latency commitments

Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft addendum. We reviewed internally (Procurement + Infra). DataWave is prepared to move forward on the following: 

- Accept Premium SLA addendum as drafted (99.95% availability, 250ms p99 on dedicated pool)
- Agreement to 12-month committed spend to start, subject to DocuSign addendum and a short runbook handoff
- We appreciate the one-time $30k migration credit — that helps internal signoff.

Ask from our side: please include SOC 2 Type II evidence (or point us to your compliance pack) and a short ops runbook (on-call contacts, escalation matrix) attached to the DocuSign packet so procurement can close. We're aiming to have the signed DocuSign envelope returned by Nov 24 so engineering can schedule the capacity change for the Jan 4 production window.

I've attached the sign-off email from our procurement lead and a SOW draft. If you can send the DocuSign link and compliance artifacts today, I'll route internally.

Appreciate the help — Priya

Priya Menon
Head of Platform Operations | DataWave
priya.menon@datawave.com

Attachments referenced: 20261110-datawave-signed-sow.pdf, procurement-signoff.pdf
